steps.title: Prepare stock and solvent standards
steps.instruction: Prepare 400 µg ml⁻¹ stock solutions of the eight rodenticides (brodifacoum, bromadiolone, chlorophacinone, coumatetralyl, difenacoum, diphacinone, flocoumafen, warfarin) in HPLC‑grade methanol. Combine appropriate volumes to make a 5 µg ml⁻¹ mixed standard (standard A). Use a pre‑purchased 10 µg ml⁻¹ difethialone methanol solution as standard B. Create an intermediate solution (solvent standard 8, 0.4 µg ml⁻¹) by mixing 1.6 ml of standard A with 0.8 ml of standard B and diluting to 20 ml with methanol. From this intermediate, prepare solvent standards 1–7 as listed in Table 1, making up each final volume with 5 mM methanolic ammonium acetate:

steps.title: Make liver‑ascorbic mixture for blank matrix
steps.instruction: Weigh four separate 50 g portions of chopped chicken liver (human‑consumption grade) into four 1 L beakers. Add 0.5 g ± 0.01 g solid ascorbic acid to each beaker and mix thoroughly with a glass rod. Add 500 g anhydrous sodium sulphate to each beaker and mix again to absorb moisture.

steps.title: Extract blank liver matrix
steps.instruction: Allow each beaker’s contents to dry for 30 min, then mix until a friable mixture is obtained. Divide each mixture equally into 250 ml extraction bottles. Add 100 ml ± 10 ml extraction solvent (1:1 v/v chloroform : acetone containing 0.075 % ascorbic acid) to each bottle, cap securely, and place on a shaker at 135 strokes min⁻¹ for at least 1 h. Filter the extract and subsequent washings through qualitative filter paper (18.5 cm) into 250 ml round‑bottomed flasks.

steps.title: Evaporate and reconstitute blank matrix extract
steps.instruction: Combine the contents of all 250 ml round‑bottomed flasks and evaporate to dryness using a rotary evaporator with a bath temperature not exceeding 40 °C. Add approximately 20 ml cyclohexane : ethyl acetate (1:1 v/v), ultrasonicate to dissolve the residue, and transfer to a 100 ml volumetric flask. Make up to volume with the same solvent mixture to obtain a blank matrix extract at 2 g ml⁻¹, ready for gel permeation chromatography (GPC).

steps.title: Prepare matrix‑matched calibration standards
steps.instruction: For each solvent standard (1–8), pipette the required volume into a 5 ml volumetric flask that already contains 0.25 ml of the blank liver matrix solution prepared above. Dilute to the mark with 5 mM methanolic ammonium acetate. This 2‑fold dilution yields matrix‑matched standards at final concentrations of 0.0005, 0.001, 0.002, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1 and 0.2 µg ml⁻¹ (matrix concentration 0.2 g ml⁻¹). Prepare fresh matrix‑matched and solvent standards every 7 days.

steps.title: Extract and clean unknown liver samples
steps.instruction: Finely chop liver tissue and weigh ≤4 g into a 100 ml beaker. Add 40 ± 1 mg solid ascorbic acid and mix with a glass rod. Add enough anhydrous sodium sulphate to absorb moisture. Dry the mixture for 20–30 min until friable, then transfer to a 250 ml extraction bottle. Add 100 ± 10 ml extraction solvent (1:1 v/v chloroform : acetone + 0.075 % ascorbic acid), cap, and shake at 135 strokes min⁻¹ for ≥1 h. Filter through qualitative filter paper (18.5 cm) into a 150 ml round‑bottom flask, evaporate to dryness (rotary evaporator, bath ≤40 °C). Re‑dissolve the residue in ~2 ml cyclohexane/ethyl acetate (1:1 v/v), transfer quantitatively to a 4 ml volumetric flask and make up to volume with the same solvent.

steps.title: Gel permeation chromatography clean‑up
steps.instruction: Filter the 4 ml extract through a 25 mm glass‑fibre syringe filter (1.2 µm). Apply 2 ml (≈2 g of extract) to a GPC column. Discard the first 60 ml of eluate, collect the next 100 ml, and evaporate to dryness using a rotary evaporator (bath ≤40 °C). Re‑dissolve the dried residue by ultrasonication in 10 ml 5 mM methanolic ammonium acetate for UHPLC‑MS/MS analysis. If the original tissue weight is considerably less than 4 g, adjust the final volume of 5 mM ammonium acetate to maintain a matrix concentration of 0.2 g ml⁻¹.

steps.title: Prepare fortified liver QC spike samples

substeps.instruction: Spike solution 1 (0.4 µg ml⁻¹): combine 1.6 ml standard A (5 µg ml⁻¹) with 0.8 ml standard B (10 µg ml⁻¹) in a 20 ml volumetric flask and fill to volume with methanol.
Spike solution 2 (0.08 µg ml⁻¹): dilute 4 ml of spike solution 1 to 20 ml with methanol.
Spike solution 3 (0.02 µg ml⁻¹): dilute 1 ml of spike solution 1 to 20 ml with methanol.
